title: Breakfast on the Beach and The Comeback
paragraphs: Sometime later, Jesus appeared to his guys again by the Sea of Galilee. Peter, Thomas, Nathanael, James, John, and two other disciples were just hanging out. Peter said, "I'm going out to fish." The other guys said, "We'll go with you." They got into the boat, but they fished all night long and caught absolutely nothing.

Right as the sun was coming up, Jesus stood on the beach, but the disciples in the boat didn't realize who it was. He called out to them, "Friends, haven't you caught any fish?" "No," they yelled back across the water. He yelled, "Throw your net on the right side of the boat and you'll find some!" They did, and instantly they couldn't even haul the net into the boat because there were so many massive fish in it! (They later counted exactly 153 huge fish, and miraculously, the net didn't tear).

John instantly recognized the miracle. He turned to Peter and said, "It is the Lord!" The exact second Simon Peter heard that, he wrapped his outer coat around himself, jumped out of the boat into the water, and furiously swam to shore. The other disciples followed in the boat, towing the insanely heavy net full of fish.

When they landed, they saw a charcoal fire already burning with fish cooking over it, and some bread. Jesus said, "Bring some of the fish you just caught." After they dragged the net ashore, Jesus said, "Come and have breakfast." None of the disciples dared to ask him, "Who are you?" They knew with absolute certainty it was the Lord. Jesus walked over, took the bread, and handed it to them, and did the same with the fish. (This was now the third time Jesus appeared to his disciples after rising from the dead).

The Restoration of The Rock After they finished eating, Jesus pulled Simon Peter aside. This is the moment Peter had been dreading but desperately needed. Remember, the last time Peter stood near a charcoal fire, he denied knowing Jesus three times.
Jesus looked right at him: "Simon son of John, do you truly love me more than these?" "Yes, Lord," Peter said. "You know that I love you." Jesus said, "Feed my lambs."
Again, Jesus asked, "Simon son of John, do you truly love me?" "Yes, Lord, you know that I love you." Jesus said, "Take care of my sheep."

The third time, Jesus asked, "Simon son of John, do you love me?" Peter was deeply hurt because Jesus asked him a third time. He said, "Lord, you know absolutely everything; you know that I love you." Jesus said, "Feed my sheep." By having Peter affirm his love three times, Jesus completely wiped out Peter's three cowardly denials. He publicly and officially restored Peter as the leader of the squad.

Jesus then gave Peter a hardcore prophecy: "I'm telling you the truth, when you were younger you dressed yourself and went wherever you wanted. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and lead you where you do not want to go." (Jesus said this to indicate the exact kind of death by which Peter would glorify God). Then Jesus looked at Peter and gave him the ultimate command: "Follow me."

Peter turned around and saw John (the disciple Jesus loved) following them. Peter pointed at John and asked, "Lord, what about him?" Jesus essentially told Peter to mind his own business: "If I want him to remain alive until I return, what is that to you? You must follow me." (Because of that comment, a crazy rumor spread among the early Christians that John was never going to die. But John clarifies right here that Jesus didn't say he wouldn't die; he just said, "If I want him to remain alive, what is that to you?").
John ends his epic masterpiece with this massive final thought:

"This is the disciple who testifies to these things and who wrote them down. We know that his testimony is true. Jesus did many other things as well. If every single one of them were written down, I suppose that even the whole world would not have enough room for the books that would be written."
